8
The acceleration of free fall on the surface of planet P is one tenth of that on the surface of
planet Q.
On the surface of P, a body has a mass of 1.0 kg and a weight of 1.0 N.
What are the mass and the weight of the same body on the surface of planet Q?
mass on Q / kg
weight on Q / N
A
1.0
0.1
B
1.0
10
C
10
10
D
10
100

hints: Notice the given pair on planet P: $m = 1.0 \text{ kg}$ and $W = 1.0 \text{ N}$ - use $W = mg$ to find $g$ on P.
Recall that mass measures amount of matter and is the same on both planets, while weight $W = mg$ changes with local $g$.
Since $g$ on Q is ten times $g$ on P, multiply the $1.0 \text{ N}$ weight on P by 10 while keeping mass at $1.0 \text{ kg}$.
walkthrough: Identify what is fixed: the same body is moved from P to Q, so its mass $m$ does not change and remains $1.0 \text{ kg}$.
State the governing relation for weight: $W = mg$, where $g$ is the local acceleration of free fall.
Find $g$ on P from the data: $g_P = W_P/m = 1.0 \text{ N} / 1.0 \text{ kg} = 1.0 \text{ N kg}^{-1}$.
Use the given ratio: $g_P$ is one tenth of $g_Q$, so $g_Q = 10 \times g_P = 10 \times 1.0 \text{ N kg}^{-1} = 10 \text{ N kg}^{-1}$.
Calculate weight on Q: $W_Q = m g_Q = 1.0 \text{ kg} \times 10 \text{ N kg}^{-1} = 10 \text{ N}$ with unit newton as required.
Combine $m = 1.0 \text{ kg}$ and $W_Q = 10 \text{ N}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Mass is correctly unchanged at $1.0 \text{ kg}$, but $0.1 \text{ N}$ would mean weaker gravity on Q, opposite to $g$ on Q being ten times larger.

B.explanation: Mass stays $1.0 \text{ kg}$ and weight becomes $m \times 10g_P = 10 \text{ N}$ because $g$ on Q is ten times that on P.

C.explanation: Weight of $10 \text{ N}$ is correct, but mass does not increase to $10 \text{ kg}$ as mass is independent of $g$.

D.explanation: Both values are wrong because mass does not scale with $g$ and $100 \text{ N}$ is ten times too large for a tenfold increase from $1.0 \text{ N}$.
